title: Final vertices characterized by right anodyne inclusions
statement: Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and weak contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Call a simplicial map right anodyne if it belongs to the smallest class containing the horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$, and all isomorphisms, and closed under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Let $J$ be a quasicategory and $t\in J_0$ a vertex. Then the inclusion $\{t\}\cong\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ is right anodyne if and only if $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is weakly contractible for every vertex $j\in J_0$.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 4.7.3.22 (02J5), equivalence (1) and (3); final object has the mapping-space meaning of Definition 4.7.3.1 in Subsection 4.7.3. Right anodyne convention: Variant 4.2.4.2, also spelled out in the proof of Proposition 4.3.6.4 (018J). Read online, not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags; Stacks does not provide this quasicategorical statement. Mapping-space convention check: Kerodon Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX), Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0), and Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5). The natural pinch-inclusion equivalences identify the right-pinched model used here with the unadorned Hom spaces used in the cited cofinality/finality statements; after taking opposites use the left-pinch comparison as well.
